messages.subject: Intro: Nora Keene (Juniper Seed) <> Aria Solano (Cedarloop)
messages.body:
Nora, Aria,

I'd like to connect you two. Aria runs Cedarloop, a maintenance-coordination product for multi-site field-service teams. Twenty-seven paying customers, honest numbers, and a founder who tells me what is not finished yet, which is rare.

Nora, you mentioned wanting capital-efficient vertical SaaS. Aria is exploring a modest seed extension. I'm not vouching for any security claim she hasn't evidence for, and she'd say the same.

I'll let you two find time.

Priya

messages.subject: Re: Intro: Nora Keene (Juniper Seed) <> Aria Solano (Cedarloop)
messages.body:
Thanks for the intro, Priya. Nora, happy to walk you through the business. We're at $39,000 MRR with 27 paying customers, 79% gross margin, and about 13 months of base runway. We're exploring a $2.5M seed extension and nothing is committed yet.

I can do Wednesday afternoon this week. Would a 30-minute call work?

Aria

messages.subject: Re: Intro: Nora Keene (Juniper Seed) <> Aria Solano (Cedarloop)
messages.body:
Aria, thanks, and thanks Priya. Wednesday the 19th at 4pm works. I'll bring questions about retention and the use of funds. Let's make it a recurring every-other-Wednesday check-in while we're both exploring this; easier than rescheduling each time.

Nora

messages.subject: Cedarloop investor update, August close
messages.body:
Hi all,

August close, all numbers reconciled with Owen:

- MRR: $39,000 (27 paying customers)
- Gross margin: 79%
- Cash: about $925,000; net burn $70,000/month; base runway roughly 13 months
- Trailing three-month NRR: 108%

Wins: Foundry Facilities (10 sites) and Harborline HVAC (6 sites) pilots are live, joined by Rivet Fleet Services (4 sites). All three are unsigned pilots and are NOT in the MRR figure above.

Risks: Enterprise buyers want SSO and a security packet; SSO is built but not approved for launch. We are not promising dates.

Asks: warm intros to field-service operators with 5+ sites, and feedback on the narrative.

Aria

messages.subject: Re: Cedarloop investor update, August close
messages.body:
Clear and honest, thank you. Please keep the pilots-vs-booked split in every update; it makes the numbers trustworthy. I'd like to see the cohort table at the next board meeting.

Ingrid

messages.subject: Re: Cedarloop investor update, August close
messages.body:
Narrative reads well. One note: "SSO is built but not approved" is the right sentence. Keep it exactly that way whenever it comes up.

Priya

messages.subject: Runway model refresh: August close
messages.body:
Aria, the August close is done. Cash $925,000, monthly net burn $70,000, base runway 13.2 months. Same assumptions as before: flat burn, no new money. I did not include any informal investor interest, per your instruction.

Model attached. The tab to look at is "Base".

messages.subject: Re: Runway model refresh: August close
messages.body: Thanks Owen. Let's add two scenarios next time: no pilot converts, and Jonah hired in November. I want the board to see both.

messages.subject: Caleb Stone, Granite Harbor <> Aria
messages.body:
Caleb, Aria: connecting you two as discussed. Caleb leads vertical-software diligence at Granite Harbor; Aria runs Cedarloop. Caleb, Aria has been refreshingly specific about what is and isn't proven.

Nora

messages.subject: Re: Caleb Stone, Granite Harbor <> Aria
messages.body:
Hi Aria, thanks Nora. I'd like to understand retention and concentration before involving a partner. Could you send cohort retention by quarter, your top-ten customer concentration, and where security readiness stands for enterprise buyers?

Caleb

messages.subject: Re: Caleb Stone, Granite Harbor <> Aria
messages.body:
Hi Caleb, happy to. Retention and concentration come from Owen's schedule, which is being finalized; I'd rather send you something reconciled than rushed. Security readiness I'll describe in plain terms: SSO is implemented, tenant-isolation evidence is in independent review, and there is no external certification. I'll send all three together.

Aria

messages.subject: Jonah West: take-home and next steps
messages.body:
Hi Aria, Dev,

Jonah has finished the infrastructure take-home. Attached are his notes. He'd like to schedule the on-site loop with Dev and the team.

Pilar

messages.subject: Re: Jonah West: take-home and next steps
messages.body: Strong on infra and reliability; a bit light on incident write-ups. I'd like to run the loop. Aria, Thursday the 24th?

messages.subject: Re: Jonah West: take-home and next steps
messages.body: Thanks Pilar. Thursday Sept 24 works. Please schedule the loop with Dev, Lena, Samira and me.

messages.subject: Alder Ridge Plumbing: cancellation notice
messages.body:
Aria,

We're a nine-person shop and the owner of the business is retiring. We're closing out the account at the end of the month. Nothing wrong with the product; thank you for the help over two years.

Colm

messages.subject: Re: Alder Ridge Plumbing: cancellation notice
messages.body:
Colm, thank you for letting me know, and congratulations to you on the retirement. We'll export all your records and delete them on your schedule. Imani will send a data export this week. Wishing you well.

Aria

messages.subject: Wedding weekend: Santa Barbara, Nov 13-15
messages.body:
Ari! Official: Santa Barbara, November 14. Bridesmaid fitting is Oct 17 at 2pm. Hotel block link is in the invite. Can you tell me by Friday if you'll make the Friday rehearsal dinner too? Pretty please say yes.

M

messages.subject: Re: Wedding weekend: Santa Barbara, Nov 13-15
messages.body: Wouldn't miss it. Yes to the rehearsal dinner, flights this week. Fitting on the 17th works; I'll move my Saturday around.

messages.subject: Pinecrest Mechanical renewal (3 sites)
messages.body:
Hi Aria,

Our annual renewal is coming up on October 31. We're happy with the dispatch board. Could you send the renewal quote for the same three sites? If there's a multi-year option, I'd like to see it.

Dana Whitlock, Pinecrest Mechanical

messages.subject: Re: Pinecrest Mechanical renewal (3 sites)
messages.body: Hi Dana, thanks for the kind words. Renewal quote attached for the same three sites. Annual prepay is available; I'll send a multi-year option once finance confirms terms.

messages.subject: Foundry: audit-log export and regional reporting
messages.body:
Aria,

Regional managers want a stable audit-log export with actor, timestamp, action and site. Today we maintain a manual weekly spreadsheet; an incomplete export would create more reconciliation work, not less. We'd also like custom regional dashboards if possible.

Ten sites, a potential paid contract of $3,000/month subject to our procurement. I can't bypass them.

Elise

messages.subject: Re: Foundry: audit-log export and regional reporting
messages.body:
Elise, thanks. The export is our top engineering priority this cycle. We will give you a sample using synthetic records plus a short note on retention and access limits, so your team can judge format before any commitment.

On custom dashboards: I'm declining a bespoke build for the pilot. We do have a regional filter; let's test whether export plus that filter covers your reporting need. If it does, we have a clean path to procurement.

Aria

messages.subject: Speaker invitation: ServiceOps Summit, Austin, Nov 17
messages.body:
Dear Aria,

We'd love for you to speak at ServiceOps Summit on "Coordinating maintenance across sites." Travel is covered for a 30-minute session on November 17.

Warmly,
The ServiceOps Summit team

messages.subject: Re: Speaker invitation: ServiceOps Summit, Austin, Nov 17
messages.body: Thank you for the invitation. I'm heading into a board meeting and a fundraise this fall, so I need to decline. Please keep us on your list for next year.

messages.subject: Dad's 65th: dinner on Oct 25
messages.body:
Honey, we booked the restaurant for Dad's birthday dinner on Sunday, October 25 at 6pm, 12 people. He doesn't know. Please don't schedule anything that evening. And bring a real jacket; it's cold by the water.

Love, Mom

messages.subject: Re: Dad's 65th: dinner on Oct 25
messages.body: Booked in my calendar already. I'll bring dessert. Not a word to Dad!

messages.subject: Business insurance renewal quote
messages.body:
Dear Aria,

Your cyber-liability and general business policy renews on November 20. The renewal quote is attached: $4,860 annually, a 4% increase. Please let us know about any change in headcount or customer data handling before renewal.

Bellwether Business Insurance

messages.subject: Re: Business insurance renewal quote
messages.body: Owen, forwarding the insurance renewal. Can you sanity-check the coverage limits against what the enterprise pilots ask for in their questionnaires? Not urgent, before Nov 1.

messages.subject: Rivet: confusing retry screen when techs lose signal
messages.body:
Aria, Imani,

Two of our technicians hit a confusing retry screen yesterday in a service bay with bad signal. They did not lose submitted work as far as we can tell, but they weren't sure and called dispatch. I care more about recovering a draft work order than about a prettier dashboard.

Before we talk contract I want to see an offline-and-reconnect walkthrough, ideally recorded, with a named owner for follow-up.

Marcus

messages.subject: Re: Rivet: confusing retry screen when techs lose signal
messages.body:
Marcus, thank you. I'm collecting the device and reconnect sequence from your two techs. Lena Ortiz owns the recovery work on our side and will do the walkthrough once the audit-log export work lands. I'll confirm which coordinators attend.

Imani

messages.subject: Re: Business insurance renewal quote
messages.body: Will do. The cyber limit is probably fine for now; I'll compare it with Foundry's questionnaire asks when Samira sends them.

messages.subject: Harborline pilot: SSO and security packet before procurement
messages.body:
Aria, Theo,

The coordinators love the dispatch board and the weekly exception digest. For procurement to authorize a paid annual contract across our six sites I need two things: SSO, and an approved security packet. Without both I can't get this past our IT group, and I'm not the only approver.

Where do we stand?

Tessa

messages.subject: Re: Rivet: confusing retry screen when techs lose signal
messages.body:
Marcus, thank you for the clear report. To be exact about what we know: no confirmed loss of submitted work, but the retry screen is confusing and we need a recorded reproduction and recovery. I'll make sure you get that, not just a promise that it's fixed.

Aria

messages.subject: Jonah West debrief, Sept 24 loop
messages.body: Debrief: Jonah would take interrupts off me and Lena for the infrastructure side. Good instincts about incident response. Concern is cost: $162,000 base is about $202,000 loaded, +$16,800/month. I'd still hire. The question is timing against the pilots.

messages.subject: Re: Jonah West debrief, Sept 24 loop
messages.body: Agreed on quality. I'm not deciding on feeling; I want Owen's forecast and at least one signed conversion first. Can you write down which interrupts a two-week reliability sprint could remove instead?

messages.subject: Q3 books close checklist
messages.body: Reminder: the Q3 close is next week. Please make sure expense receipts and the contractor invoices are uploaded by September 30.

messages.subject: Re: Q3 books close checklist
messages.body: All contractor invoices are in. Only two receipts left; I'll chase them.

messages.subject: Re: Harborline pilot: SSO and security packet before procurement
messages.body:
Tessa, great news: SSO is ready for enterprise rollout. Samira will send the security packet this week and we'll get you on a paid annual contract quickly. $1,500/month for all six sites.

Theo

messages.subject: Jonah West: compensation and timing
messages.body:
Aria, Jonah's expectations are in line with what we discussed: $162,000 base plus standard equity, start in November. He's weighing another offer and asked for a decision by the end of next week.

Pilar

messages.subject: FSW #212: Technician shortages and what dispatchers do about them
messages.body:
This week in field service:

- The shrinking pool of qualified HVAC technicians and how multi-site teams are rebalancing work.
- A look at offline-first mobile workflows in places with poor signal.
- Reader mailbag: how do you handle after-hours escalations?

Read online. Unsubscribe any time.

messages.body:
Hello,

We'd like to add two more sites to our Cedarloop account starting in November. Please send the updated order form.

Ravi Menon, Bluehollow Property Services

messages.subject: Quick question about your dispatch software
messages.body:
Hi Aria,

I help service companies cut drive time by 18% with Routewise. Do you have 15 minutes this week for a quick demo?

Brent

messages.subject: Re: Bluehollow: adding two more sites
messages.body: Thanks Ravi, wonderful. Order form attached; onboarding for the new sites takes about a week. I'll set up a kickoff.

messages.subject: Granite Harbor follow-ups: cohorts, concentration, security
messages.body:
Aria, checking in. For me to sponsor an internal partner introduction I need the cohort appendix and a qualified security status. No rush on a decision from us; I just want the materials to be solid.

Caleb

messages.subject: Non-binding interest and use of funds
messages.body:
Aria,

Great call today. To put in writing what I said: across Juniper's network I've heard informal interest of roughly $350,000 toward your seed extension. To be explicit, that is non-binding, nothing here is a term sheet, and nobody has approved anything. I'd rather you plan as if it were zero.

What would move me from interested to concrete:
1. Evidence that at least one of the three pilots converts to a signed contract.
2. A use-of-funds plan by line: engineering, security, go-to-market.
3. The cohort table Ingrid asked for, and a customer concentration view.

Can you send an update with these early next week?

Nora

messages.subject: Re: Non-binding interest and use of funds
messages.body:
Nora, understood, and thank you for being so direct. We model the forecast with zero from the round. I'll send the update Monday (Oct 12) with pilot status, a use-of-funds sketch, and the cohort and concentration schedules Owen is finalizing.

On pilots: two of three are blocked on evidence we owe them (security packet and audit-log export), not on interest. I'd rather show you the real blockers.

Aria

messages.subject: Seed extension documents: template review
messages.body:
Aria,

I've reviewed the draft seed-extension template you forwarded. Notes:

1. Nothing has been signed and I haven't seen a term sheet. The materials should not use the words "committed" or "closing" for any investor yet.
2. The use-of-proceeds clause should match the plan you give Nora; I'd keep security and audit-log work as named items.
3. Add a sentence that product statements (SSO, export) are descriptions of current status, not warranties.

Redline attached.

Hana

messages.subject: Re: Granite Harbor follow-ups: cohorts, concentration, security
messages.body:
Caleb, thanks. The update lands Monday the 12th and will include both. I'll mark anything unfinished as unfinished.

Aria

messages.subject: Re: Seed extension documents: template review
messages.body:
Thanks Hana, these all make sense. Accepting 1 and 3. On 2, I'll confirm the line items after Owen's forecast is final and send them to you. No investor has committed, so none of this is urgent, but I want the paperwork right before anyone asks.

Aria

messages.subject: Rivet reconnect sequence: details from the techs
messages.body:
Aria, Lena,

Sequence from Rivet's two techs: (1) start a work order offline, (2) background the app for about 20 minutes, (3) return with signal restored, (4) retry screen appears with the draft still showing. Both devices were on the same OS version. Screenshots attached.

I'd like Lena to reproduce it before we walk Marcus through anything.

Imani

messages.subject: Re: Jonah West: compensation and timing
messages.body: Pilar, thanks for the clear timeline. I won't approve anything until the forecast is reviewed. I'll give you a transparent update this week and will not leave you guessing.

messages.subject: Re: Rivet reconnect sequence: details from the techs
messages.body: Got it. I can reproduce steps 1 to 3 on the test device. The recovery path works, but the retry screen reads like an error. I'll write it up after the export block. Walkthrough: Friday afternoon is possible if the export hours are protected first.

messages.subject: Pilot adoption: weekly coordinator usage
messages.body: Weekly adoption: Harborline 5 of 6 sites active weekly; Rivet 3 of 4 (three dispatch coordinators repeat-using); Foundry 8 of 10. The dispatch board is the most-used feature; the exception digest is opened by 80% of coordinators. I'd call Rivet the strongest candidate for a first signature if the offline walkthrough goes well.

messages.subject: Pipeline recap, week ending Oct 2
messages.body: Quick recap: three unsigned pilots ($6,500 MRR combined at quoted terms, none booked). New inbound: Bluehollow expansion (two more sites), plus one new demo request from a regional HVAC group. Churn risk: Alder Ridge Plumbing gave notice.

messages.subject: Re: Pilot adoption: weekly coordinator usage
messages.body: That's useful, thank you. Let's review it together Wednesday and decide what proof each pilot needs before talking contracts.

messages.subject: Re: Wedding weekend: Santa Barbara, Nov 13-15
messages.body: The dress arrived and it's gorgeous. Also: farmers market next Saturday? I'll get coffee.

messages.subject: NRR benchmarks for vertical SaaS, Q3
messages.body: SaaS Metrics Digest: median trailing-three-month NRR for sub-$5M ARR vertical SaaS companies came in at 104% this quarter. Top quartile starts at 111%. Methodology and cohorts inside.

messages.subject: Board meeting Oct 22: scorecard deck
messages.body:
Aria, the board meeting is Thursday Oct 22, 10am, at the usual spot. Could you send the scorecard deck by Friday Oct 16 so I can read it over the weekend? I'd like the agenda to be: (1) booked vs. pilot revenue, (2) runway and the Jonah hiring question, (3) security path, (4) the fundraise.

Ingrid

messages.subject: Re: Board meeting Oct 22: scorecard deck
messages.body:
Ingrid, will do. Deck out Friday Oct 16. I'll lead with the booked-versus-pilot split ($42,000 MRR booked; $6,500 pilot pipeline unsigned) and a runway view with and without the infrastructure hire. Owen is finishing the no-conversion case.

Aria

messages.subject: Foundry security questionnaire: answers needed
messages.body:
Foundry's questionnaire has 64 questions. I can answer 41 from existing docs. The remaining 23 are about tenant isolation, access logging and retention, and need Dev or Aria to confirm facts. I will not mark unresolved controls complete.

List attached. Can we get Dev 30 minutes this week?

messages.subject: Re: Foundry security questionnaire: answers needed
messages.body: I can do Wednesday 2:30pm. I'll answer the isolation and logging ones. Retention defaults are still Aria's call.

messages.subject: Your annual membership renews Oct 20
messages.body:
Hi Aria,

Your Ironwood Strength Club annual membership renews on October 20 ($780). No action needed. Morning lift crew meets Mon/Wed/Fri at 6:45am as always. To make changes, reply to this email.

messages.subject: Proposal: 30% off year one + unlimited sites for all three pilots
messages.body:
Aria, Owen,

To close the three pilots faster I'd like to offer 30% off the first year and unlimited sites on each contract. Harborline, Rivet and Foundry all say price isn't the issue but timing is, and a strong offer would pull them forward.

Theo

messages.subject: Re: Seed extension documents: template review
messages.body:
Understood. I've reserved an hour on my calendar for the week of the 19th. Send the line items when you have them.

Hana

messages.subject: Meeting hygiene: merging Pricing review into Pipeline review
messages.body: Tuesdays and Thursdays are four meetings back to back and the last one is usually the one that falls over. Can we merge Pricing review into Pipeline review? Also, Ops standup could be async on Thursdays.

messages.subject: Re: Meeting hygiene: merging Pricing review into Pipeline review
messages.body: Yes to both. Let's try it starting this week and see whether the last slot still gets cancelled.

messages.subject: Re: Rivet: confusing retry screen when techs lose signal
messages.body:
Checking in. We're still four sites in the pilot and the techs like the drafts. Any update on the walkthrough date? Contract talk waits for it.

Marcus

messages.subject: Re: Proposal: 30% off year one + unlimited sites for all three pilots
messages.body: I'd decline. Unlimited sites gives away the expansion lever, and a temporary 30% hides the economics: at the quoted packages, year-one revenue would fall from $78,000 to about $55,000 across all three, before any cost to serve extra sites. If we need a timing incentive, tie it to something we control.

messages.subject: Security packet v3: wording check
messages.body:
Packet v3 is in the shared drive. The wording I most want you to read is the paragraph on external standards. I wrote: "Cedarloop has not completed an external compliance certification. Internal controls are mapped to common frameworks for reference only." If Priya hasn't signed off, we can't say more.

Okay to send with that sentence?

messages.subject: Re: Harborline pilot: SSO and security packet before procurement
messages.body:
Thanks Theo. Procurement is asking for a rollout date and an SSO test window. Can you give me both, and the name of the person on your side who owns the security packet?

Tessa

messages.subject: Re: Security packet v3: wording check
messages.body: Yes, keep that sentence exactly. No SOC 2 mention beyond it. And leave the unresolved controls marked unresolved; a clean status update beats a false green checklist.

messages.subject: Re: Foundry: audit-log export and regional reporting
messages.body:
Understood on the dashboard. We can try export plus the regional filter. Please send the sample when it's ready; our regional managers meet next Thursday and I'd like it in front of them.

Elise

messages.subject: Audit-log export: plan v1 and the four-hour block
messages.body:
Aria,

Export plan v1 attached. Phases: (1) schema: actor, timestamp, action, site name and ID; (2) archived-site edge case; (3) synthetic sample labeled as synthetic; (4) retention default and access notes. I need one uninterrupted four-hour block (10:00-14:00) to finish phases 1-3. Could you protect it and send me the revised export plan with your decisions on retention and what counts as "done"? I'll start on that.

Lena

messages.subject: Hold on Harborline dates (SSO wording)
messages.body:
Theo, Samira,

Tessa asked for a rollout date. We don't have one. SSO is implemented, but it is not approved for enterprise rollout until tenant-isolation review and the audit-log export evidence are done. Theo, your Sept 28 note to her said "ready for enterprise rollout". Please don't send anything else on dates.

Samira, can you draft the correction? Language: implementation exists, launch approval is pending sign-off, no fixed date, no certification claim. Name Dev as owner of the isolation evidence, Priya as independent reviewer, and yourself as owner of the packet.

I'll review before it goes to Tessa.

Aria

messages.subject: Re: Audit-log export: plan v1 and the four-hour block
messages.body: Lena, this is great. Two decisions now: default retention 13 months and configurable per tenant; "done" is an export Foundry accepts plus a named procurement next step. I'll send you the revised plan that adds both, plus the Harborline dependency, on Monday. The 10-14 block is protected.

messages.subject: Re: Proposal: 30% off year one + unlimited sites for all three pilots
messages.body:
Decision:

1. No 30% discount and no unlimited sites. Nothing is sent as final terms.
2. Counterproposal: a maximum 10% annual prepay incentive, only after scope and security obligations are settled.
3. Quotes stay as they are: Harborline $1,500/month (6 sites), Rivet $2,000 (4 sites), Foundry $3,000 (10 sites). These are three negotiated packages, not a per-site price list.
4. Theo, a one-page package and site-limit table to me by Friday the 16th. A pilot-success milestone is fine as a timing lever; custom dashboards are not.

Aria

messages.subject: Re: Hold on Harborline dates (SSO wording)
messages.body:
On it. Draft by end of day. I'll also add the procurement-owner question (who signs on their side) and a proposed review slot so the next step isn't just "wait".

Theo, can you confirm you'll hold the 3-sites-at-a-time rollout idea until Dev signs off?

messages.subject: Re: Hold on Harborline dates (SSO wording)
messages.body: Understood, my mistake. I overreached on the SSO wording and I'll hold dates. I'll route anything about timing through Samira from here.

messages.subject: Reference check summary: Jonah West
messages.body: Three references done, all positive: calm in incidents, writes runbooks, mentors well. One caution: he prefers stable roadmaps. Details in the shared doc. Nothing blocks an offer; the open question is cash, not candidate.

messages.subject: Re: Pinecrest Mechanical renewal (3 sites)
messages.body: We'll renew on the annual terms. Please send the paperwork and we'll sign this week.

messages.subject: Tenant-isolation evidence summary v2
messages.body:
Aria, evidence summary v2 attached. 212 synthetic cross-tenant access tests, 210 pass; two exceptions, neither blocks, both need a written disposition (Priya flagged them). Raw logs are in the evidence folder. I am not claiming a certification, just what the tests show.

You wanted to forward it to Priya; this is the copy to send.

messages.subject: Re: Hold on Harborline dates (SSO wording)
messages.body: Draft correction attached for your review. Tone: honest and still warm. It's not sent.

messages.subject: Re: Tenant-isolation evidence summary v2
messages.body: Thanks Dev. I'll forward to Priya once you've written the dispositions for the two exceptions. Can you add them to the doc by Monday?

messages.subject: Re: Board meeting Oct 22: scorecard deck
messages.body:
Good. One request: a single slide on what you'd cut if no pilot converts. I'd rather talk about it now than in January.

Ingrid

messages.subject: Isolation review: scope and what I will sign
messages.body:
Aria, Dev,

Happy to review the isolation evidence. Scope for me: the test design, the two exceptions, and whether the dispositions are reasonable. I will give you a written disposition, not a blanket certification, and I won't sign a compliance statement based on a demo. I can start Wednesday once the evidence arrives.

Priya

messages.subject: Harborline SSO check-in: Mon Oct 12, 7:00 AM PT
messages.body:
Invitation: Harborline SSO check-in
When: Monday, October 12, 7:00-7:30 AM Pacific
Where: Video call (link in the calendar invite)
Who: Tessa Cole (organizer), Aria Solano, Samira Vale

Tessa wants a date for the SSO evidence packet before procurement meets Wednesday. Our ops team starts early, so 7am is the only slot this week.

messages.subject: Re: Jonah West: compensation and timing
messages.body: Understood. Jonah asked me to pass on that he's still keen. If you can say whether a decision is likely before October 16, that would help him plan.

messages.subject: Re: Granite Harbor follow-ups: cohorts, concentration, security
messages.body:
Sounds good. Holding the partner calendar slot for the week of the 19th in case the materials are ready. To be clear, that is a placeholder, not a commitment either way.

Caleb

messages.subject: Cash forecast draft: no-conversion and hire cases
messages.body:
Aria,

Draft forecast attached. Headlines:

- Today: cash $840,000, net burn $70,000/month, 12.0 months.
- Hire case (Jonah, about $202,000 loaded, +$16,800/month): burn $86,800, runway about 9.7 months.
- No-conversion case: pilots stay unpaid, so no change to the base; the hire case then drives the floor.
- Signed-contract-only case: counts Harborline $1,500, Rivet $2,000 and Foundry $3,000 per month only after signature, and not before.

Cash floor trigger is $500,000, a planning line, not a covenant. In the hire case we cross it around month 4 if nothing is signed.

Can we walk through it Monday? I still owe you the cohort and concentration schedule for Caleb.

Owen

messages.subject: Pipeline recap, week ending Oct 9

messages.subject: The boring metric that predicts renewals
messages.body:
Founder Notes, issue 87.

Most early-stage teams track signups. The better predictor of renewal: the share of accounts where at least three people use the product each week. We looked at 40 companies and the pattern was stark.

Also in this issue: how to write an investor update that doesn't bury the bad news.
